report.source_text: The procedure was well tolerated and the patient had an unremarkable post procedure recovery. He remained pain free with no further PR bleeds during his hospital admission and was discharged home 24 hours post embolization. The following week at home was also unremarkable.

clinician.final_diagnosis: CT Abdomen done on the day of admission showed a 6 mm cystic artery pseudo aneurysm.
clinician.trajectory_summary: An 83-year-old male presented with acute PR bleed and syncope. Initial labs showed a drop in hemoglobin from 11.9 to 10.2 mg/dL within 24 hours, indicating significant blood loss. A CT Abdomen performed on admission revealed a 6 mm cystic artery pseudoaneurysm and a thick-walled gallbladder with surrounding inflammatory changes, inseparable from the hepatic flexure. The cystic artery pseudoaneurysm was treated with coil embolization via an endovascular approach. Following the procedure, the patient had an unremarkable recovery, experienced no further PR bleeds during hospitalization, and was discharged home 24 hours post-embolization, with an unremarkable course the following week.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with acute PR bleed and syncope, with a history of acute cholecystitis 5 weeks prior.
Initial complete blood count showed a drop in hemoglobin from 11.9 mg/dL to 10.2 mg/dL within 24 hours, while other initial labs were unremarkable.
CT Abdomen on the day of admission showed a 6 mm cystic artery pseudoaneurysm and a thick-walled gallbladder with surrounding inflammatory changes, inseparable from the hepatic flexure of the colon.
The cystic artery pseudoaneurysm was treated with coil embolization via an endovascular approach.
Following embolization, the patient had an unremarkable recovery with no further PR bleeds and was discharged.

The outcome of the planned elective cholecystectomy is not documented.
